profile.summary: DeepSequence learns a generative model of one protein family from a multiple sequence alignment, with no labels and no experimental measurements. It is a variational autoencoder: the alignment is compressed to a small latent space and decoded back to a distribution over sequences. Once fitted, it scores the effect of a mutation by how much less probable the mutated sequence is than the wild type, and it can also supply features for supervised learning or generate new sequences.

summary_quotes.text: DeepSequence is a generative, unsupervised latent variable model for biological sequences. Given a multiple sequence alignment as an input, it can be used to predict accessible mutations, extract quantitative features for supervised learning, and generate libraries of new sequences satisfying apparent constraints.
we show how it is possible to capture higher-order, context-dependent constraints in biological sequences via latent variable models with nonlinear dependencies
The model, learned in an unsupervised manner solely on the basis of sequence information, is grounded with biologically motivated priors

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A model is fitted to one alignment at a time. The training example builds a VariationalAutoencoder over the alignment: an encoder of two layers of 1500 units, a latent space of 30 dimensions, a decoder of 100 then 500 units, a convolutional final layer of width 40 with 4 patterns, and a sigmoid output with a learned scale. Sequence weights are computed from the alignment before training. The example runs 300,000 stochastic variational inference updates. The published idea is that this nonlinear latent variable model captures dependencies among many residues at once, where pairwise models capture only covariation between pairs.

quotes.text: It models higher-order dependencies in sequences as a nonlinear combination of constraints between subsets of residues.
Recent approaches have demonstrated benefits of including interactions to capture pairwise covariation, but leave higher-order dependencies out of reach.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There is no versioned release and no checkpoint family. The repository holds one implementation, read at commit fd5c272b, and the fitted parameters are per protein family: the example script downloads pretrained parameters for beta-lactamase, a PDZ domain and PABP. A result must therefore name the alignment, the random seed and the number of updates, not a checkpoint name. The example fixes the seed at 12345 and trains for 300,000 updates on the BLAT_ECOLX alignment.

sections.title: Alignments and data
sections.body: The input alignment matters as much as the model. The developers advise building alignments with their EVcouplings package, though any alignment can be used, and they publish the alignments from the paper as a single download. Pretrained parameters for three families come from the same server at Harvard Medical School.

quotes.text: we advise that alignments be generated with the [EVcouplings package](https://github.com/debbiemarkslab/EVcouplings), though any sequence alignment can be used

run_guide.summary: Get the code at the pinned commit, download the paper's alignments and pretrained parameters, then fit a model on the beta-lactamase alignment.
prerequisites: Python 2.7 with Theano 1.0.1, per the README. The INSTALL file points to the Anaconda 2.7 distribution and the Theano instructions.
A GPU is advised but not required; CUDA must be installed separately for GPU use.
An alignment of the target family. The developers advise building it with EVcouplings.
